title: The fulfillment of eternal things through daily life
english: He who begins to build this tower, as if starting with the foundation, should complete the building as if placing a crown upon the roof, lest he suffer shame before those passing by, who are accustomed to mocking those who have not completed the citizenship they undertook.

A connection can be made to 'Lead me from the face of the enemy' (Ps 60:6b) and 'You have led me in a straight path thus'; 'You have led me from the face of the enemy' has become my hope, but also a tower of strength in leading me from the face of the enemy. The hope of the saints is the true and unshakeable Savior, as Paul says, 'Jesus Christ of our hope' (1 Tim 1:1), and the prophecy upon him is that they hope in him; for he himself, having been foretold, shall be the expectation of the Nations. Someone, having been perfected in holiness for the ages in that dwelling, signifies 'Who shall dwell in your holy habitation?' (Ps 60:7); for this is the same eternal one in the tabernacle, the Lord, and not man. Although such a tabernacle does not possess the perfection of the Holy of Holies, there is no state with it surpassing the rational ones in which they shall be in Father and Son, but rather in the Trinity. Therefore, it is said to dwell for the ages, but not to reside in the dwelling. He who has become in this [dwelling] shall be covered under the shelter of the wings of God.

For he says, 'You are very rich, and you provide great gifts' (Ps 60:7), rather, by freely giving to perfect men the becoming of your sons, you have given them an inheritance. For although it is expected to be given according to the resurrection in the future age, it is nonetheless being given in a favorable way to those who are being led according to the time what is necessary. And to those who fear his name, God has given an inheritance (Ps 60:8). If there is a difference between those fearing God and his name, and those believing in him and in his name—since it is often said that those made intimate by the approach of God, those united to him, the God, are inferior—it is seen that the inheritance is given also to those fearing God; for if grace has been increased to the inferior, much more to those who have ascended far above. Whoever obtains the interpreted gifts, what kind of king is he, according to what is signified regarding the God-fearing ones as they were a Kingdom...

A beloved, a holy nation. By this signified thing to reign, and the apostles, expecting, say to the Corinthians, 'You reigned without us, let us also reign with you.' To the reigning which has happened, there is added by the Lord, 'day by day occurring.' For it is necessary from a preceding state of light to a transition into another likewise, so that the eternal things, concerning which it is said, 'And I remembered the eternal and meditated upon them' (Ps 103:2), might be fulfilled from that which is named of the days. And the life of the days is extended by taking them day by day, as generations of generations before God.

Who will seek out His mercy and truth? Often, of the divine teachings, His mercy is joined with the truth of God. For since to know clearly and purely the truth of God is not possible for one surrounded by human weakness, from this there is a need of the mercy of God in order to understand the truth. This contributes to the fore-set purpose, that all men should be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth. For first, it is necessary to be saved by the mercy of God, so that subsequently the knowledge of the truth may exist. For the salvation of men is the work of the mercy of God. 'For God sent His mercy and His truth,' and the following.

Since in whom I have found a thankful reception from You, I will sing in Your name, praising through works, thoughts, and good words the prophecy of You called upon me (Ps 60:8); and with this I will repay day by day, just as Jacob says, 'If God gives me bread to eat,' and the following, 'all things to me shall be mine if I tithe them to You' (Gen 28:20-22). For before these words it is brought forward, 'Jacob made a vow,' saying, 'If the Lord be with me,' as 'I will tithe them.' And also to say 'repaying prayers day by day' and 'singing in the name of God unto the age of ages,' for the one singing in the name [is] the one being praised, to extend into the coming age; but the one repaying the prayers, it is as if the time being fulfilled of the days is being completed; it is not that which is delayed by each individual's life. Since we are not in [this] life, we shall repay the prayers, so that we also may sing unto the age of ages in the name of God.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Deception of the Enemy and True Repentance
english: That we may be able. Everyone shifting from virtue into vice is shaken (Ps 61:3), but this does not happen abruptly; a disturbance first occurs in the thoughts through the passions, so that if appropriate action is taken, the shaken thoughts do not become a collapse and a fall.

For when an ugly desire or some other irrational movement begins, the pious thought must intervene, grasping God, to direct the impulse toward action, so that a greater shaking does not occur. The Savior clearly teaches this in the Gospel, uprooting the beginnings of sins so that their remaining does not result in a greater practical shaking.

He who is established and rooted in love is an unshakable wall and has a firmly set hedge (Ps 61:4c); how then could those passing by the way, wicked men and evil powers, not strike it? God surrounds him with such a secure hedge, saying, 'I have plowed and set a hedge.' For this hedge consists of angels guarding, and of truths of dogmas, and of actions being performed according to virtue. While this remains, no one will be able to harm the divine fruits of the spiritual plant. But if the one guarding the vineyard should ever bring forth thorns instead of grapes, God, abandoning him, says, 'I will take away his hedge and it shall be for plunder, and I will pull down his wall and it shall be for trampling.' If this happens because of the production of bad fruit from us, the wall is leaned and the hedge is pushed.

The honor of the wise, which the wicked plot to cast away, is virtue and piety (Ps 61:5), according to 'Glory and honor and peace to everyone working the good' (1 Clem 1:1). Therefore, vice is a dishonor, in which those who have fallen, feeling they have suffered, say, 'Our dishonor has uncovered us unto tribulation' (Ps 61:5). To this, man also takes part, not understanding the value of being in honor. Since the deceivers lying in wait cannot draw one into vice by force, they say, 'They did not drive away my honor, but they plotted to cast it away'; for they are not those who can overcome the one standing strongly against them. Related to these are those about whom Paul writes, 'Deceiving through flattering speech and lying words the hearts of the innocent' (2 Cor 11:14).

It is of the same mind: 'If your enemy entreats you with a great voice, do not be persuaded [Ps 61:7]; for seven evils are in his soul, perhaps coming from the seven spirits, as the unclean spirit receives from more evil spirits than himself.' ...as if he were entreating for the seven evils existing in his soul, the First [God] saying brightly and pleasantly in a punishing way, 'do not be persuaded'; for blessing with the mouth, he curses the heart.

I will not repent, becoming a repentant one by sinning and being distanced from God [Ps 61:8], according to what is written concerning Jacob, who was overwhelmed and turned away from God his savior. Grasping God, I have not become a repentant one, they attain salvation and glory upon God; for I was not saved by my own power or art. And he says 'glory upon God' because it is that which the only God gives to those seeking him, and 'salvation' not of the flesh but of the rational soul, which the one having believed into the Trinity possesses, according to what is said, 'Finishing the faith, the salvation of souls.' Therefore, even if he is violently thrust back into error, I make hope upon him, who has often saved me.

All the assemblies of the peoples of the nations who have believed [Ps 61:9], who no longer have God and hope, hope in him against all craftiness, making your hearts manifest before him; for God will become a helper to you. The same is meant by to pour out before him the heart, to love him from the whole soul and the whole heart. For often to pour out has been arranged instead of a rich abundance and a lavish supply, as in 'the love of God is poured out in the hearts of you through the Holy Spirit' [Rom 5:5].

To such people it was said [Ps 61:10], 'Why do you love vanity and seek falsehood, even though you are commanded not to have a small and a great weight, but a true scale, since a double weight is an abomination to the Lord.' It must be said whether these things are intended, and also toward those who have dealings and fellowship; for in every matter, justice is desired; for those running together toward vanity vainly strive, always having a vain agreement and zeal. title: The Twofold Circumcision and the True God
english: They are dying men who are no longer gods and sons of the Most High, as it is signified by what is written: 'For where there is strife and jealousy among you, are you not fleshly and walking according to man?' (James 3:16).

For it is not possible to serve God and mammon, nor indeed to hope for injustice and God (Matthew 6:24). If it seems that the wealth of one who does not seize and does not act unjustly is flowing and diminishing, it is not necessary to add to the heart, so that the heart might not be grieved by the diminishing of the money.

Because the name of injustice signifies, on the one hand, inequality regarding exchanges and sharing, as in 'But you do wrong and deprive even your brothers,' and on the other hand, all practical wickedness, as it is said, 'I hated injustice and detested it' (1 John 3:15), so one must watch according to what the meaning of the word now presents. One says the former, making it clear through the fact that plunder and flowing wealth were accompanying him, while the other says the latter, as it is said, 'But he who loves injustice.' For this is the case, since injustice is not entirely one thing, nor is the seizing regarding money.

God is incorporeal, rather existing beyond all generated being, both material and intellectual, having nothing entangled with himself; thus, when God speaks, He speaks once, that is, monoidly and uncomposedly, not as I hear Him thus anymore. For what is spoken once, you hear as two, according to the manifestation; for this voice is a pointing voice.

He therefore says such a thing: as He speaks with a pure intellect and an uncomposed voice, I hear the things spoken as being two, with my imagination standing by, perceiving someone called a spoken word which turns out to be unspeakable, as He speaks with intellect and an uncomposed voice. And so, if the apostle, writing that he has heard unspeakable words (2 Corinthians 12:4), wishes to present this, the unspeakable ones are such that they are heard not by grasping syllables and sounds, but also by words being present, because the intellect possesses the truth. For where the truth is, there is a proposition. And it is necessary for the proposition to be from a name and a word.

And it must be said otherwise: we use vocal organs, and we are unable to say many things at once. Of God, speaking once and all at once, we hear doubly. Stop, lest it be possible to say a third. Of God, commanding once concerning sacrifice, we hear the command both sensuously and spiritually.

Just as we understand circumcision in two ways, once spoken by God: the bodily and the spiritual. Whether the Father is God, and the Son is Lord, and the Word stands among these, or whether the same God is both God and Lord, saying, 'Visit now' (Ps 62:2a); for what is being viewed is both pious and true in both respects. It is necessary to seek how he gives to each according to his works. For if the sufferings of the present time are not worthy of the glory that is about to be revealed (Rom 8:18), and he who has worked only trifles is not punished worthily. For if one observes iniquities, 'Lord, Lord, who will endure?' (Ps 69:1), how must one take [judgment] by equality? One must oversee lest it becomes not according to quantity but according to quality; and quantity is indicated by the word, the greater things of value being given praiseworthily to the righteous and the punishment being diminished. For equality is not according to corrective justice, but according to distributive justice, the equal and the unequal.

This is accomplished for the one who has come out of ignorance and malice, as 'The night has passed, and the day has approached' (Ps 62:2a). To this, 'Out of the night my spirit watches for you, O God' (Ps 62:2b) is conjoined. But if someone does the works of the night and darkness, how can he say 'I watch at dawn' without the dawn standing before him? And 'I watch toward you' is not to be heard locally. For God is not in a place, but in a disposition, becoming a relationship toward God by having leaped over the sensible things; for to this follows coming toward God. And also the saying, 'God, the God of mine.' For the God of the saints worshipping him is God once and for all, not of all those who have the 'is', but of some who have been set free. Therefore, the belly of those having desire for luxury is not simply called God; nor even the demons are strictly gods of the Gentiles, though called gods. God alone, and every truly wise man will say by nature and truly to God, 'God, the God of mine.'

'From all those present, let my longing depart' (Ps 62:3); I thirst with the soul to be toward God, a spring of water stretching toward me, changing into eternal life (Ps 62:3).
